enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance). Compared to last month, El Niño strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0°C, extending farther westward across the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean [Fig. 1] . The Niño indices increased, reaching +2.5°C in Niño-3.4, +3.6°C in Niño-3, and +4.4°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained significantly above average [Fig. 3] , associated with a deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Convection and rainfall remained enhanced from the central to the eastern Pacific, while suppressed conditions persisted over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were consistently negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected the ongoing evolution of El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen before beginning to weaken in early 2027 [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MST Wed Nov 25 2026

Another chilly night ahead across Southern New Mexico and Far 
West Texas as winds remain very light, allowing temperatures to 
dip into the lower-to-mid 30s. Broken cirrus moving in from the 
west will keep skies partly cloudy overnight.

Quiet weather on Thanksgiving Day as temperatures remain cool. 
Lowland highs in the upper 50s/lower 60s will run slightly below 
normal for late November, but only by a few degrees. Wind will be
almost non-existant. High clouds clearing during the morning hours
will be followed by sunny skies in the afternoon and overnight.
Looks like a great day for holiday festivities.

A warmup is in store to finish the week with light west surface 
winds 5 to 10 mph and a subtle increase in heights aloft. Lowland 
highs will warm to the lower-to-mid 60s Friday afternoon, then 
warm further to the lower 70s on Saturday. 

80-knot 500mb jet streak over the Four Corners on Saturday will 
move down the front of the ridge aloft, crossing through Central 
New Mexico. Lee surface low formation across the Southern High 
Plains will allow for breezy conditions locally Saturday 
afternoon. West winds 15 to 25 mph with peak gusts to 40 mph is 
currently the most likely outcome. Will need to monitor for 
stronger gusts along the east slopes of the Sacramento Mountains, 
Black Range, and mountain gaps during that timeframe. Forecast is
currently not reaching Wind Advisory criteria, but will be close 
enough to watch over the next few days.

A weak cold front behind this system will knock temperatures back
down to normal (lowland highs lower 60s) on Sunday. This looks to
be a brief cool down and quick rebound headed into next week with
dry and zonal flow over the region Monday/Tuesday.

GFS and ECMWF deterministic solutions are in good agreement 
resolving a deeper upper low over the Western U.S. sometime next 
week (December 2 to 4). This would be our next shot at 
precipitation chances. Right now, slight chance of lowland rain 
chances and snow chances above 7000 feet AGL is the forecast. 

&&

VFR conditions with light winds and some passing high clouds.

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 622 AM MST Thu Nov 26 2026

Fine weather, but poor vent rates for today and Friday. A weak 
disturbance will graze northern and eastern New Mexico on Saturday,
with breezy west winds developing. A few gusts over 40 mph will be
possible in exposed areas in the Sacramento Mountains and the 
Black Range. Lowland deserts may see RH values reach 15% Saturday
afternoon, but ERC values remain quite low due to abundant autumn
precipitation, despite the more recent dryness.
